title: Think and Grow Rich
author: Napoleon Hill
blurb: Napoleon Hill says he spent years studying hundreds of successful people, prompted by the industrialist Andrew Carnegie, to find a shared formula for achievement. The result is thirteen principles, starting with the idea that every fortune begins as a thought. Hill argues you need a burning desire for a specific goal, written down with a deadline and a plan, and repeated daily until your subconscious believes it. He stresses that knowledge only matters when organized into action, that imagination turns ideas into plans, and that a small group of allies, which he calls a Master Mind, multiplies your power. Quick decisions and stubborn persistence carry you past setbacks, and Hill warns that fears such as poverty and criticism quietly sabotage most people. His core claim is that mindset, applied with discipline, shapes results.

lessons.t: Every Fortune Starts as a Burning Desire
lessons.b: Hill argues achievement begins with an intense, specific desire, illustrated by Edwin Barnes, who resolved to become Thomas Edison's business partner and eventually did.

lessons.t: Six Steps to Turn Wishes into Goals
lessons.b: Hill's method turns a vague wish into a definite goal: name an exact amount, decide what you will give, set a date, make a plan, write it down, and read it aloud twice daily.
